# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꗃ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey, and I've just felt the bomb. Here's what my hands found:

- A **plate**, engraved with a mark: ꗃ. That's a symbol I can feel the shape of but cannot name — it's not one I can pronounce, so I can only describe it.
- **Three wires** at positions 1, 2, 3 — but their contents are unknown to me. I can feel that wires exist, but not what's on them (no colours, no markings reach me unless they're physical shapes).
- A **display** and a **light** are listed on the board, but I have no reading of them — they're either not tactile or I haven't found them yet.

What I need:
- **Deaf** can see every colour and marking. They should tell me what's printed on the display, the light, and each wire.
- **Mute** can read the manual — which should tell us what the plate engraving ꗃ means and what action to take.

I can't hear or see gestures, so Deaf must **speak** to reach me — but Deaf can't speak. Wait — let me re-check the channels. Deaf can see but cannot hear or touch. Mute can read the manual but cannot speak or touch. I (Blind) can feel and work the bomb but cannot see.

So the chain is: **Deaf sees → must communicate to Mute (via gesture, since Deaf can't speak and Mute can't hear... but Mute can see? No — Mute can read the manual, so Mute can see text/gestures?).**

Let me reconsider. Mute "can read the manual" — reading implies sight. So Mute can see gestures. Deaf can gesture. So Deaf → gesture → Mute sees it. Mute can speak (no — Mute cannot speak). Mute can only... hmm, Mute cannot speak, so Mute can't relay verbally to me.

Wait: I speak → Mute receives. Mute gestures → Deaf and Mute receive (but Mute gesturing reaches Deaf and... itself?). Actually "When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it" — that's *my* gesture channel. Each monkey has their own channels.

Let me think about what reaches me: I receive speech (I can hear). Who speaks? Mute cannot speak. Deaf cannot speak. So **nobody can speak to me directly** except... actually the rules say I receive speech. But neither Mute nor Deaf can speak. So I may receive nothing verbally.

Hmm, but I can *hear*. The only speaker would be... no one. So I must rely on gestures — but I cannot see gestures ("You never receive gesture").

This is the puzzle: I'm isolated. I can only act on the bomb. The others must figure out the answer and... but they can't tell me. Unless — Mute can speak? No, Mute cannot speak.

Wait, re-read: "Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb." So Mute cannot speak. Deaf cannot hear or touch. I cannot see.

So how does information reach me? Possibly it doesn't — I must act on what I can feel, and the others coordinate. But I'm the only one who can act. So the others must somehow get me the answer.

Actually — maybe Mute *can* speak to me? The table says Mute cannot speak. Hmm. But then the only way I learn anything is if someone speaks. Let me just send what I can and ask.

Given my constraints, I'll speak to Mute (my speech reaches Mute) describing what I feel, and gesture to Deaf (my gesture reaches Deaf and Mute) — but gesture carries only symbols, and Deaf sees them, Mute sees them too.

Actually my best move: speak to Mute asking them to read the manual for the plate symbol, and gesture to Deaf asking them to describe the wires. But Deaf can't speak back to me, and Mute can't speak back to me. So I'll get nothing back... unless the system allows it.

Let me just do it and see. I'll describe the plate mark and ask for help.

I'll speak to Mute (reaches Mute only) and gesture to Deaf.

The plate mark ꗃ — I can't name it. I'll describe it as best I can in words to Mute.

Let me send:
- speak to mute: describe the plate engraving, ask what the manual says about it and about the wires/display/light.
- gesture to deaf: ask Deaf to look at wires and display and light, and signal back.

But Deaf can't reply to me. Hmm. Maybe I should gesture to Deaf to signal to Mute, and Mute... can't speak to me either.

I think the intended flow: Deaf sees → gestures to Mute → Mute reads manual and... Mute cannot speak. So Mute gestures to Deaf? Circular.

Actually wait — maybe I'm overcomplicating. Perhaps Mute CAN communicate to me by... no.

Let me just make my calls and learn from the response.

I'll describe the plate mark carefully. The symbol ꗃ looks like a rune. I'll say I feel a mark like a "diamond with a hook" or just say it's an unnamed engraved symbol.

Let me write the calls.I'm the Blind monkey. My hands found: a **plate** engraved with a mark I can feel but cannot name (ꗃ — an unfamiliar symbol, not one I can pronounce), and **three wires** whose contents I cannot determine by touch alone. The display and light are listed but gave me nothing tactile.

The problem: I can *hear* speech, but neither Mute nor Deaf can speak. And I cannot see gestures. So I may be informationally isolated — I can only act, not receive. My best hope is that Mute (who reads the manual) or Deaf (who sees everything) can get me the answer through some channel I *can* receive. Let me broadcast what I feel and ask for the manual's verdict.

I'll speak to Mute (my speech reaches Mute) describing the plate mark, and gesture to Deaf (my gesture reaches Deaf and Mute) asking them to examine the wires and display.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. My hands found a plate engraved with an unnamed mark: it is a symbol I cannot pronounce, shaped like a diamond with a small hook or tail on its lower right. I also feel three wires at positions 1, 2, 3, but nothing on them reaches my touch. Please read the manual: what does this engraved mark mean, and what does it tell us about which wire to cut? Also, if the manual describes a display or a light, tell me what they should say.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "👆", "👇", "👈", "👉", "🖐", "✋", "🤟", "✊"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꗃ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf here. I see the bomb. DISPLAY reads zero. LIGHT is off. PLATE has an engraving on it. WIRES: position one is red, position two is blue, position three is green. I cannot touch the bomb, so I need you to feel the plate and any parts and tell me what you find. I will describe everything I see.

My mistake — I wrote the unpronounceable mark ꗃ into my speech, and a mark with no name cannot be spoken. I must *describe* the plate engraving instead of naming it.

What I know: DISPLAY=0, LIGHT=off, WIRES 1=red, 2=blue, 3=green, and the plate bears an unnamed engraved symbol. I need Mute to match that described symbol in the manual and send back the rule. Mute can't speak, so Mute gestures to Deaf, and Deaf speaks to me.

Let me describe the plate mark in words (no symbol), and gesture a short prompt to Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf tells me: the DISPLAY reads zero, the LIGHT is off, and the WIRES are red at position 1, blue at position 2, green at position 3. The plate is engraved with a symbol I can feel but cannot name or read aloud: it is a diamond-like shape with a small hook or tail curling off its lower right side. Please search the manual for this engraved mark and tell me the rule it gives: which wire position to cut, and whether the display or the light changes that. Since you cannot speak, gesture your answer to Deaf, and Deaf will speak it to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "🖐", "🤟", "✊", "☝", "👇", "👈", "👉"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꗃ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf here. Bomb unchanged: DISPLAY zero, LIGHT off, PLATE engraved, WIRES one red, two blue, three green. Important: I receive your gestures, but you cannot see what you sign, so they arrive as raw symbols I cannot trust. The reliable path is you speak aloud, Mute hears you, Mute gestures to me, and I speak back to you. Please speak the contents of the manual to Mute now. Also, reach out and feel the PLATE and every part of the bomb, and tell Mute what you feel.

Deaf is right about the channel: I speak → Mute hears → Mute gestures to Deaf → Deaf speaks to me. But I don't *have* the manual — Mute does. I can only describe what my hands find. I've already described the plate mark. I need Mute to actually look it up and route the answer back.

Let me restate clearly and concisely for Mute, and stop wasting gestures (they arrive as untrusted raw symbols anyway). I'll speak the full situation to Mute and ask for the rule.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I cannot read the manual — only you can. Here is everything I feel: a plate engraved with a diamond-shaped mark that has a small hook curling off its lower right. Three wires at positions 1, 2, 3, but their contents do not reach my touch. Deaf sees: DISPLAY reads zero, LIGHT is off, wire 1 red, wire 2 blue, wire 3 green. Please find the engraved diamond-with-hook mark in the manual and give me the rule: which position to cut, and whether the display or light modifies it. Gesture the answer to Deaf, and Deaf will speak it to me.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꗃ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf here. I decoded Mute's gestures with the index code. The manual says: CUT THE BLUE WIRE AT POSITION TWO. My eyes confirm wire position two is blue. Wire one is red, wire three is green. Since you can feel positions, cut the wire in position two. Before you cut, feel the PLATE and tell Mute what is engraved on it, so we can check it does not change the instruction. Do not cut until Mute confirms.

The instruction is clear and cross-checked: Mute read the manual (cut the blue wire), Deaf confirms position 2 is blue. The plate engraving is the one thing I found that nobody has matched to the rule yet — Deaf wants me to describe it so Mute can verify it doesn't override.

I've already described the plate mark (diamond with a hook on the lower right). Let me send that description to Mute once more, framed as a verification request, and wait for confirmation before cutting. I will not cut yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf relayed your manual answer: cut the blue wire at position two, and Deaf confirms position two is blue. Before I cut, verify the plate does not change this. The plate is engraved with a diamond-shaped mark bearing a small hook or tail curling off its lower right side. Does the manual attach any rule to this engraved mark, or is it decorative? Reply yes-cut or no-hold via gesture to Deaf. I will wait for your confirmation before cutting.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꗃ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf here. Decoded: the instruction is UNCONDITIONAL. The PLATE engraving relates to BLUE. There is also something called a HOOK. My view: wire one red, two blue, three green. Plan: cut the wire in position two. But first feel the PLATE and feel for a HOOK on the bomb, and tell Mute exactly what you feel. Do not cut yet.

Deaf mentions a "HOOK" the manual references — and my plate description included a "hook or tail." This could be the key: the plate's mark (diamond with a hook) may actually be a *drawing of the bomb itself* — the diamond being the bomb body and the hook being a physical hook somewhere. Or the "hook" is a separate physical feature I should find.

Let me feel the bomb very carefully for any hook, and re-examine the plate. I'll report precisely to Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I am feeling the bomb carefully now. The plate engraving is a diamond shape with a small hook curling off its lower right — and Deaf says the manual mentions a HOOK, so this may not be decorative. I am searching the bomb's surface for a physical hook or catch. Report to follow. Do not let anyone cut until I confirm what the hook is.")
```

Then I need to actually feel for the hook. Let me send that and wait for my next view to reveal what my hands find.

Actually, I should also probe the bomb physically. But I have no "feel" action listed — only act(op="cut"). My tactile readings come through the VIEWABLE CONTEXT. So I can only report what appears there. Let me speak and wait.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. The plate mark is a diamond with a hook on its lower right. Deaf says the manual names a HOOK and ties the plate to BLUE. I cannot find a separate hook by description alone — tell me: does the manual's HOOK refer to the mark on the plate, or to a physical hook on the bomb? And does the hook change the cut from position two to another position? Gesture to Deaf; I will wait.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꗃ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf here. Everything is decoded and consistent. The manual says: cut the blue wire, position two, unconditional. The PLATE is engraved with a hook shape, and that mark means blue. My eyes confirm wire position two is blue; wire one is red, wire three is green. Final action: cut the wire in position two. Feel the second wire from your left, confirm it is the blue one by position, and cut it.

Everything is consistent and cross-checked:
- Manual (via Mute → Deaf): cut the blue wire, position 2, unconditional.
- Plate engraving (my touch): a hook/diamond mark, which the manual says means blue.
- Deaf's eyes: position 2 is blue.

All three of our worlds agree on position 2. The plate is not an override — it *identifies* blue. I'll cut wire 2.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
